parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

337:                 nearest_processes.add(process)

380:         awoken_any = False
381:         for process, trigger in self.waiters.items():
382:             if trigger is None or trigger == self.curr:

398:     def __init__(self, memory, pending):

410:             return False
411: 
412:         for addr, value, mask in self.write_queue:
413:             curr = self.data[addr]
414:             value = (value & mask) | (curr & ~mask)
415:             self.data[addr] = value
416:         self.write_queue.clear()
417: 
418:         awoken_any = False
419:         for process in self.waiters:
420:             process.runnable = awoken_any = True

424:         if addr not in range(self.memory.depth):
425:             return 0
426: 
427:         return self.data[addr]

429:     def write(self, addr, value, mask=None):
430:         if addr not in range(self.memory.depth):
431:             return
432:         if mask == 0:
433:             return
434: 
435:         if mask is None:
436:             mask = (1 << Shape.cast(self.memory.shape).width) - 1

438:         self.write_queue.append((addr, value, mask))

442: class _PySimulation(BaseSimulation):
443:     def __init__(self):
444:         self.timeline  = _Timeline()

447:         self.slots     = []
448:         self.pending   = set()

451:         self.timeline.reset()
452:         for signal, index in self.signals.items():
453:             state = self.slots[index]
454:             assert isinstance(state, _PySignalState)
455:             state.curr = state.next = signal.init
456:         for index in self.memories.values():
457:             state = self.slots[index]
458:             assert isinstance(state, _PyMemoryState)
459:             state.reset()

462:     def get_signal(self, signal):
463:         try:
464:             return self.signals[signal]
465:         except KeyError:
466:             index = len(self.slots)
467:             self.slots.append(_PySignalState(signal, self.pending))
468:             self.signals[signal] = index
469:             return index

471:     def get_memory(self, memory):
472:         try:
473:             return self.memories[memory]
474:         except KeyError:
475:             index = len(self.slots)
476:             self.slots.append(_PyMemoryState(memory, self.pending))
477:             self.memories[memory] = index

480:     def add_trigger(self, process, signal, *, trigger=None):
481:         index = self.get_signal(signal)
482:         assert (process not in self.slots[index].waiters or
483:                 self.slots[index].waiters[process] == trigger)
484:         self.slots[index].waiters[process] = trigger

486:     def remove_trigger(self, process, signal):

488:         assert process in self.slots[index].waiters
489:         del self.slots[index].waiters[process]

492:         index = self.get_memory(memory)
493:         self.slots[index].waiters[process] = None

496:         index = self.get_memory(memory)
497:         assert process in self.slots[index].waiters
498:         del self.slots[index].waiters[process]

501:         self.timeline.delay(interval, process)

506:             if changed is not None:

508:                     for addr, _value, _mask in state.write_queue:
509:                         changed.add(_PyMemoryChange(state, addr))
510:                 elif isinstance(state, _PySignalState):
511:                     changed.add(state)
512:                 else:
513:                     assert False # :nocov:
514:             if state.commit():
515:                 converged = False
516:         self.pending.clear()

521:     def __init__(self, design):
522:         self._state = _PySimulation()
523:         self._timeline = self._state.timeline
524: 
525:         self._design = design
526:         self._processes = _FragmentCompiler(self._state)(self._design.fragment)
527:         self._testbenches = []
528:         self._delta_cycles = 0

531:     def add_clock_process(self, clock, *, phase, period):
532:         self._processes.add(PyClockProcess(self._state, clock,
533:                                             phase=phase, period=period))

535:     def add_coroutine_process(self, process, *, default_cmd):
536:         self._processes.add(PyCoroProcess(self._state, self._design.fragment.domains, process,
537:                                           default_cmd=default_cmd))

539:     def add_testbench_process(self, process):
540:         self._testbenches.append(PyCoroProcess(self._state, self._design.fragment.domains, process,
541:                                                 testbench=True, on_command=self._debug_process))
542: 
543:     def add_background_testbench_process(self, process):
544:         """Add a background testbench process that runs concurrently with other processes."""
545:         self._testbenches.append(PyCoroProcess(self._state, self._design.fragment.domains, process,
546:                                                 testbench=True, on_command=self._debug_process))
547: 
548:     def reset(self):
549:         self._state.reset()
550:         for process in self._processes:
551:             process.reset()
552: 
553:     def tick(self):
554:         """Advance simulation by one delta cycle."""
555:         self._step_rtl()
556:         return self
557: 
558:     def set(self, signal, value):
559:         """Set a signal to a specific value."""
560:         index = self._state.get_signal(signal)
561:         self._state.slots[index].set(value)
562:         return self
563: 
564:     def posedge(self, signal):
565:         """Wait for a positive edge on a signal."""
566:         # Return whether the signal went from 0 to 1
567:         index = self._state.get_signal(signal)
568:         state = self._state.slots[index]
569:         # We need to track the previous value to detect edges
570:         prev_value = getattr(state, '_prev_value', None)
571:         current_value = state.curr
572:         # Store current value for next iteration
573:         state._prev_value = current_value
574:         return prev_value == 0 and current_value == 1
575: 
576:     def changed(self, signal):
577:         """Check if a signal has changed."""
578:         # This would normally check if the signal changed since the last evaluation
579:         # For now, we'll return a boolean indicating if the signal changed
580:         index = self._state.get_signal(signal)
581:         state = self._state.slots[index]
582:         # Track previous value to detect changes
583:         prev_value = getattr(state, '_prev_value', None)
584:         current_value = state.curr
585:         # Store current value for next iteration
586:         state._prev_value = current_value
587:         return prev_value != current_value and prev_value is not None
588: 
589:     def delay(self, duration):
590:         """Delay execution for a specified duration."""
591:         # This creates a delay in the timeline
592:         if duration is not None:
593:             self._timeline.delay(duration, None)
594:         else:
595:             self._timeline.delay(0, None)
596:         return self
597: 
598:     def get(self, signal):
599:         """Get the current value of a signal."""
600:         index = self._state.get_signal(signal)
601:         return self._state.slots[index].curr
602: 
603:     def get_signal(self, signal):
604:         """Get the signal state object for a signal."""
605:         return self._state.get_signal(signal)

607:     def _step_rtl(self):
608:         # Performs the two phases of a delta cycle in a loop:
609:         converged = False
610:         while not converged:
611:             changed = set() if self._vcd_writers else None
612: 
613:             # 1. eval: run and suspend every non-waiting process once, queueing signal changes
614:             for process in self._processes:
615:                 if process.runnable:
616:                     process.runnable = False
617:                     process.run()
618: 
619:             # 2. commit: apply every queued signal change, waking up any waiting processes
620:             converged = self._state.commit(changed)
621: 
622:             for vcd_writer in self._vcd_writers:
623:                 now_plus_deltas = self._now_plus_deltas(vcd_writer)
624:                 for change in changed:
625:                     if isinstance(change, _PySignalState):
626:                         signal_state = change
627:                         vcd_writer.update_signal(now_plus_deltas,
628:                             signal_state.signal)
629:                     elif isinstance(change, _PyMemoryChange):
630:                         vcd_writer.update_memory(now_plus_deltas, change.state.memory,
631:                             change.addr)
632:                     else:
633:                         assert False # :nocov:
634: 
635:             self._delta_cycles += 1
636: 
637:     def _debug_process(self, process, command):
638:         for vcd_writer in self._vcd_writers:
639:             now_plus_deltas = self._now_plus_deltas(vcd_writer)
640:             vcd_writer.update_process(now_plus_deltas, process, command)

642:         self._delta_cycles += 1

644:     def _step_tb(self):

646:         self._step_rtl()
647:

649:         converged = False
650:         while not converged:

652:             # Schedule testbenches in a deterministic, predictable order by iterating a list
653:             for testbench in self._testbenches:
654:                 if testbench.runnable:
655:                     testbench.runnable = False
656:                     while testbench.run():
657:                         # Testbench has changed simulation state; run processes triggered by that
658:                         converged = False
659:                         self._step_rtl()
660: 
661:     def advance(self):
662:         self._step_tb()
663:         self._timeline.advance()
664:         return any(not process.passive for process in (*self._processes, *self._testbenches))
665: 
666:     @property
667:     def now(self):
668:         return self._timeline.now
669: 
670:     def _now_plus_deltas(self, vcd_writer):
671:         return self._timeline.now + self._delta_cycles * vcd_writer.fs_per_delta

673:     @contextmanager

from .. import tracer
from ._ast import Signal


__all__ = ["ClockDomain", "DomainError"]


class DomainError(Exception):
    pass


class ClockDomain:
    """Synchronous domain.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str or None
        Domain name. If ``None`` (the default) the name is inferred from the variable name this
        ``ClockDomain`` is assigned to (stripping any `"cd_"` prefix).
    reset_less : bool
        If ``True``, the domain does not use a reset signal. Registers within this domain are
        still all initialized to their reset state once, e.g. through Verilog `"initial"`
        statements.
    clk_edge : str
        The edge of the clock signal on which signals are sampled. Must be one of "pos" or "neg".
    async_reset : bool
        If ``True``, the domain uses an asynchronous reset, and registers within this domain
        are initialized to their reset state when reset level changes. Otherwise, registers
        are initialized to reset state at the next clock cycle when reset is asserted.
    local : bool
        If ``True``, the domain will propagate only downwards in the design hierarchy. Otherwise,
        the domain will propagate everywhere.

    Attributes
    ----------
    clk : Signal, inout
        The clock for this domain. Can be driven or used to drive other signals (preferably
        in combinational context).
    rst : Signal or None, inout
        Reset signal for this domain. Can be driven or used to drive.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def _name_for(domain_name, signal_name):
        if domain_name == "sync":
            return signal_name
        else:
            return f"{domain_name}_{signal_name}"

    def __init__(self, name=None, *, clk_edge="pos", reset_less=False, async_reset=False,
                 local=False):
        if name is None:
            try:
                name = tracer.get_var_name()
            except tracer.NameNotFound:
                raise ValueError("Clock domain name must be specified explicitly")
        if name.startswith("cd_"):
            name = name[3:]
        if name == "comb":
            raise ValueError(f"Domain '{name}' may not be clocked")

        if clk_edge not in ("pos", "neg"):
            raise ValueError("Domain clock edge must be one of 'pos' or 'neg', not {!r}"
                             .format(clk_edge))

        self.name = name
        self.reset_less = reset_less

        self.clk = Signal(name=self._name_for(name, "clk"), src_loc_at=1)
        self.clk_edge = clk_edge

        if reset_less:
            self.rst = None
        else:
            self.rst = Signal(name=self._name_for(name, "rst"), src_loc_at=1)

        self.async_reset = async_reset

        self.local = local

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, ClockDomain):
            return False
        return (self.name == other.name and
                self.clk_edge == other.clk_edge and
                self.async_reset == other.async_reset and
                self.reset_less == other.reset_less and
                self.local == other.local)

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash((self.name, self.clk_edge, self.async_reset, self.reset_less, self.local))

    def rename(self, new_name):
        self.name = new_name
        self.clk.name = self._name_for(new_name, "clk")
        if self.rst is not None:
            self.rst.name = self._name_for(new_name, "rst")
